title: Cliff Jackson's piano roll and his child prodigy flyer
summary: She took Cliff's piano roll of 'Hock Shop Blues' to the Hall of Fame, and has a 1909 flyer from when he was a boy pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I took a piano roll of his down to the Hall of Fame, "The Hock Shop Blues,"
No kidding. I remember we had one of those in our house many years ago.
You pumped it with your foot?

Oh, yeah. But you know what, I took it down there and I put the roll on and actually you know what, you could use this to Pete's piano because you can watch the holes in the roll and watch the keys and it's a very -- of course, "Hock Shop Blues" is just another blues but I was looking at it and you know, anybody could just sit down and look at that roll and just know what keys to hit. It's really great.
How many years had Cliff played piano?
Oh, Cliff, listen, I've got a flyer his brother gave me after Cliff passed. No, in fact, he sent it up before Cliff passed. It's a picture of Cliff in a little white Fontleroy suit
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
with curls, made in December 1909. He was born in 1902, so he was a child prodigy, you know what I mean?
And it says, whatever his grandmother's name was, "Presenting Master Cliff Jackson, child prodigy in concert," at one of the churches down there.
